title: `abs(MIN)` and `divide(MIN, -1)`
description: DuckDB raises `Out of Range Error: Overflow …` for `abs(-2⁶³)` and `-2⁶³ // -1` (native).
reference: Substrait and the reference: `abs` and `divide` on `i8`…`i64` return the same type; with `overflow` omitted, `abs(MIN)` and `MIN / -1` raise.
Lean: no finding. `verify` reports `overflow` as an error for both.

evidence.note: TryAbsOperator: int8_t, int16_t, int32_t, int64_t and hugeint_t specialisations raise `Overflow on abs` at the minimum
abs on TINYINT … HUGEINT binds TryAbsOperator
PropagateAbsStats swaps in the unchecked AbsOperator only when the input's statistics exclude the minimum

provenance.notes: `abs(MIN)` raises on every signed width; each width has its own specialisation, so the reading covers i8, i16 and i32 as well.

evidence.note: abs of test_all_types()'s tinyint, smallint, int, bigint and hugeint columns (their first row is the type's minimum) raises `Overflow on abs`; `WHERE {type} > 0` runs
`MIN // -1` raises at TINYINT, SMALLINT, INTEGER and BIGINT; `(MIN + 1) // -1` gives the maximum

provenance.notes: The abs test runs every signed width, so it pins `int.abs` overflow at i8, i16 and i32 as at i64.
